Document.project_name: Erosion Protection Project
City of Kingston, New Public Boat Launch Installation on Colonel By Lake
location: Rideau Canal National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: The City of Kingston is proposing to install a new public boat launch on Colonel By Lake within Cecil Graham Park. The dimensions of the proposed pre-cast concrete boat launch are 8 m wide x 23 m long and the location is situated within a natural bay (Esther March Bay). The total in-water footprint is expected to be ~416m2. Additional in-water site alteration plans include a new 3 x 22 m floating dock. Additional upland site alteration plans include a 3 x 2 m concrete headwall to support an access ramp to the dock, a shoreline path, picnic area, parking lot and driveway.

Document.project_name: Haley Brook Crossing Replacement
Document.description: The Haley Brook Crossing Replacement project is proposed to address the long-term deterioration of the existing twin culvert crossing located along Shepody Road within Fundy National Park. In the fall of 2024, significant erosion was identified between the two culverts, compromising approximately 40% of their length and creating a void in the road surface measuring approximately 1.2m by 1.0m by 0.6m. Emergency stabilization measures, including the placement of sandbags and riprap, were implemented to reduce erosion and maintain roadway safety. While these temporary measures have proven effective in preventing further deterioration, they do not provide a sustainable long-term solution, and ongoing erosion remains a concern. The proposed project is to replace the existing failing twin culvert crossing with a single open bottom arch culvert that will provide a safe, resilient, and reliable crossing for park operations, visitors, and the public. The replacement structure will restore stream stability and accommodate natural hydrological processes while reducing the risk of future infrastructure failures and associated maintenance requirements.

Document.project_name: Site Remediation at Heart's Content SCH, NL
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada – Real Property and Environmental Management (DFO-RPEM)
location: Heart's Content SCH is located in Heart's Content, Newfoundland (NL). Located in the southern Avalon Peninsula
Document.description: Install a soil/gravel cap over the upland portion of the site to eliminate the exposure pathway of contaminants that have been identified in soil at the site. The primary contaminant is PAHs. The cap will consist of an engineered, structural pavement ready pad consisting of a geomembrane liner, proof rolled rockfill subgrade and granular subbase and base layers, and possibly grass cover over a portion of the site. The installation of the cap will also include measures to prevent coastal erosion (e.g., heavy rock).

Document.project_name: Road Paving Program, various locations, Prince Edward Island National Park
location: Prince Edward Island National Park of Canada
Document.description: Parks Canada is proposing improvement works on roadways, parking lot and associated infrastructures within Prince Edward Island National Park: Wild Rose Lane, Dalvay Crescent, Ross Lane, Ross Lane beach access and Cavendish Grove access. The project will include reparation of pavement on paved road, new pavement on gravel road, road widening and development of new access road. The project scope also includes reparation of pavement on parking lot, parking lot extension/migration and the replacement/installation of culvert. Work will be conducted with heavy equipment from within the road and parking lot footprint.

Document.project_name: On-Farm Composting System, Pilot Project
Document.description: This pilot project proposes the establishment of an on farm composting system to help address orchard waste management challenges. Project will reduce landfill hauling requirements, and improve sustainability and nutrient cycling on-farm. Project will involve the installation of approximately 200 meters of electric fence and gate, as well as approximately 200 meters of underground pipeline to distribute water to the area from an existing source.

Document.project_name: Lucky Man Cree Nation Cultural Centre and Site Servicing
Document.description:
Lucky Man Cree Nation  is proposing to build a new cultural centre, including a traditional knowledge sharing space, a future ceremony building, and associated pathways and access road. The project is intended to provide cultural spaces and amenities, as well as the required water and sewer systems to accompany these spaces. To service the building, a site servicing plan has also been developed, including a septic field (pipes), water cistern, trenches, and septic tank.

Site prep will include minor vegetation clearing and grubbing, as well as excavation and earthworks (grading). Construction will include excavation and drilling for the septic field, and construction (above-ground) of the traditional knowledge sharing space. Landscaping, re-seeding, and tree planting will also be completed surrounding the knowledge sharing space.

Document.project_name: Sorel-Tracy Port Terminal Project
Document.description: QSL International Ltd. is proposing the construction and operation of a new port terminal in the industrial-port zone of Sorel-Tracy, Quebec. As proposed, the Sorel-Tracy Port Terminal Project would include a new floating wharf and related intermodal infrastructures. The project would support the handling of bulk materials, such as fertilizer and road salt, as well as general cargo, such as oversized steel parts, and would accommodate approximately 35 ships per year.

Document.project_name: Sumas Multiplex
Document.description:
This project will build a new, culturally relevant, multi-purpose community and recreation facility (approx. 18,740 sq.ft [~1741 m2]) for the Sumas First Nation community, serving on-reserve residents and open to the general public. The facility will include a community hall/gymnasium, boardroom, hydrotherapy room, large kitchen, fitness centre, and pedestrian bridge over the neighbouring creek.

Based on the location (a former Brick plant land = ~16, 918 m2), a new design concept is being developed to accommodate the building infrastructure. The project location is within the boundaries of the Upper Sumas No 6 Reserve lands.


	Large site area (~6.59 acres)
	Increased capacity
	
		~18,000 ft2 multiplex facility
		~12,000 ft2 office space
		~240 parking spaces
		Over 1 acre of open green space
		Future expansion are (~1.34 acres)
	
	


Works for this project are also associated with Registry posting 80963 - relating to the remediation of the the old Brick plant on the site.

Document.project_name: Recreational dock dredging - 5345 Indian River Drive
Document.proponent: upland owner at 5345 Indian River Dr.
location: Recreational dock dredging - 5345 Indian River Drive
Document.description:
The proposed project

The project includes dredging of up to 2-metres of accumulated sediment around a recreational dock at the above noted property to prevent structural damage. The sediment accumulated during a late-2024 weather event which caused debris to flow down an adjacent stream and fill in the area around the project site's recreational dock.

The works include mobilizing a long-reach excavator to the foreshore, digging along the impacted side of the dock, and removing up to 1,000-cubic metres of sediment. The sediment would be placed upland, off port jurisdiction, for reuse in landscaping or upland disposal pending approval from the District of North Vancouver.

An Environmental Monitor will be on site during the works to ensure no impacts to fish or marine mammals, and to conduct turbidity monitoring of the exclusion zone. Sediment controls will be in place if deemed necessary.

The excavator will be upland in the dry, and works will take place during low tide only. No other in-water works are proposed, and no works related to the recreational dock are included in this application. The proposed project will take place within the least-risk fisheries window of August 16 - February 28 and will take 2-5 days to complete.

Document.project_name: Construct Modular Office Complex, Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Edmonton, AB
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Edmonton will be receiving 2000+ additional troops over the coming years and there is a deficit of office space, which will need to be met in spring of 2027. Infrastructure required to accommodate the 250-personnel modular office space has an estimated total gross interior floor area of 6,000 m2 and an exterior space of 9,000 m2 for parking and storage. The site is currently landscaped and mowed regularly during the growing season so there's no habitat for species at risk.

Document.project_name: Army Training Centre – Central (ATC-C) Meaford Staff Accommodation (M-202) Upgrades
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Real Property Operations proposes renovating Building M-202, located at Army Training Centre – Central (ATC-C) Meaford to address deficiencies and to allow for continued use of this facility. The project will include mechanical upgrades, such as removal of old boiler and installation of new boiler, heat pump and split Air Conditioning units, architectural upgrades, such as exterior repairs, new interior flooring, painting, new countertops and attic hatches, as well as electrical upgrades, such as new light fixtures, fire alarms, Carbon dioxide (CO2) detectors, and new electrical panel. Lastly, the proposed project will include the excavation of a trench for the installation of an underground electrical feeder line measuring approximately 125m in length which will be connected to building M-203. Any excess fill will be managed in accordance with federal and provincial requirements, with an intent to re-use in the trenches.

Document.project_name: Pump Station Demolition- 3rd Canadian Division Support Group (CDSG), Detachment British Columbia Mainland - Chilliwack
location: 3rd Canadian Division Support Group (CDSG), Detachment British Columbia Mainland - Chilliwack
Document.description:
There is a small, unused pumphouse on Department of National Defence (DND) land owned by Greater Vernon Water Utility. The pump house is 5.5 m x 8 m in size and is surrounded by a chain-link fence, which will also be removed. The entire project area including access from the nearby paved area is approximately 200 m². A hazardous material assessment was completed, and these materials will be removed prior to the pump house structure being demolished. The fence posts will be pulled from the ground without additional digging.

BC. Real Property Operations Unit Pacific det Chilliwack is carrying out an assessment and Species at Risk permitting in order to support the North Okanagan Regional District, who will carry out the demolition.

Document.project_name: Main Camp Utilities Upgrade at Vernon Military Camp
Document.description:
A Utilities upgrade project for the Vernon Military Camp (Main Camp) is planned to start construction in spring 2025.

The work will involve the excavation and disposal of existing underground utility lines, installation of new water, sewer and storm lines, installation of a backbone communication duct system, restoration of roads, grading, repaving and revegetating impacts areas within the Main Camp of Vernon Military Camp. In addition to the work occurring at the Main Camp, an existing concrete chamber on the west side of Okanagan Highway 97 will have the valves permanently closed, the abandoned meter removed and disposed of, the chamber cut down to a minimum of 1.0 m below grade, backfilled and abandoned. Both of these areas where work will be occurring are cumulatively referred to as the "Main Camp Project Area".

Document.project_name: Terminated: Pump Station Demolition - 3rd Canadian Division Support Group (CDSG), Detachment British Columbia Mainland - Chilliwack
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing to remove a number of facilities over time. The Regional District of North Okanagan (RDNO) owns the Greater Vernon Water Utility (GVWU), and a number of these facilities are no longer in use. As a result, funding has been created to remove these facilities over time. The DND pump station is a small building located on DND land just off highway 97 when entering Vernon from the South. A demolition contractor has been secured for the work and plans to remove the small building (5.5m by 8m). The Project is approximately a 2 to 3 day project. The prime contractor will mobilize on site, review unexploded explosive ordnance (UXO) protocols with Notra, remove hazardous materials prior to demolition. Once the site is cleared of UXO and hazardous materials contractor will remove the building and chain link fence and legally dispose of non-recyclable materials.

Document.project_name: Department of National Defence (DND) NORAD A-OTHR (Arctic Over the Horizon Radar) Project at Military Aeronautical Communications System (MACS) Carrying Place
Buffalo River Dene Nation Stage 5 Subdivision
location: BUFFALO RIVER DENE NATION RESERVE NO. 193
Document.description:
The Buffalo River Dene Nation is proposing to construct a new subdivision to meet the community's need for current and future housing units. The proposed Stage 5 subdivision will provide up to 50 new lots and will occupy approximately 15 hectares of forested land. New infrastructure required as part of the subdivision includes high density polyethylene (HDPE) water main pipeline, polyvinyl chloride (PVC) sewer main pipeline and manholes, water and sewer service lines, hydrants, roadways and drainage culverts, power and phone utilities.

Clearing and grubbing of the site is proposed to occur in the fall or winter to avoid the risk of harming migratory nesting birds. The extent of vegetation clearing will be kept to the minimum amount necessary to construct the new subdivision and to provide a fire break. Activities during construction include primary earthworks, new utility installation, sub grade construction, ditch construction, grading and landscaping.

Document.project_name: Radio Observatory – 5762 Akins Road
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Defence Research and Development Canada intends to install a radio observatory consisting of up to approximately 1,000 antennas, consisting of vertical metal poles of approximately 6 metres in height, spread over an area of up to 60 hectares. The antennas will be connected to a central control shelter by wires. The proposed site will also include security fencing to control access.

The radio observatory will be a receiving station that will be used to assess the direction-of-arrival of radio signals in the high frequency band, from transmit stations at other locations in Canada.

The radio observatory builds on capabilities demonstrated by previous similar large-scale high frequency receive arrays built at the same site, such as the sampled aperture receive array that was active at the site in the 1980s. The radio observatory will be receive-only and will not emit radio signals nor produce any radiofrequency hazards.

location: 275 Point Petre Road, Cherry Valley, Prince Edward County,

Document.project_name: Deep Bay Parking & Pedestrian Access
location: Riding Mountain National Park of Canada
Document.description: Project Objective: During busy periods, the demand to access Deep Bay by vehicle, bike and foot traffic is more than what the existing infrastructure can accommodate. The parking lot can become hazardous for visitors due to overcrowding of vehicles and the inability of Wasagaming Drive to safely accommodate two-way traffic and parking. Project description includes creating a new gravel parking lot on the south side of TaWaPit Drive (can accommodate 38 vehicles) in a previously disturbed area, with a pedestrian access corridor and road crossing from the parking lot to the Deep Bay Area. Construction of the new parking lot and access corridor will require removal of vegetation and top organic layer, followed by placement of granular fill. Signage and highway painting will complete this phase. Following construction activities, Wasagaming Drive from the West Intersection with TaWaPit to the existing parking area will be closed to vehicular traffic, open only to bikes and pedestrians. Another pedestrian crossing will be painted where the new east ramp of the Lakeshore Trail intersects with this section of Wasagaming Drive.

Document.project_name: Brandon Dispatchable Capacity Project
location: East Brandon Industrial Area within the City of Brandon
Document.description: Manitoba Hydro is proposing the expansion of an existing natural gas-fueled electricity generating facility, located in Brandon, Manitoba. As proposed, the Brandon Dispatchable Capacity Project would include the development of three new simple-cycle combustion turbines, with an anticipated increase in production capacity of approximately 750 megawatts. Project components would also include a 32-kilometre natural gas pipeline, two electrical transmission lines totalling 3.5 kilometres, and upgrades to the existing electrical transmission station. The project is expected to operate for about 30 years.

Document.project_name: ATCO pipeline 1147151 - 1550 - ALT - Tsuut'ina Medical Centre
Nashwaak Fish Counting Station Access Road Repair and Upgrade
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada, Real Property and Environmental Management

Document.project_name: Ermineskin Cree Nation On-Reserve Water Supply Project
Document.description:
Ermineskin Cree Nation is proposing to construct Phase I of an On-Reserve Water Supply Project. The project will include the construction of 1.3 km of waterline from the Nation boundary to a new water reservoir and pump station and the dormancy of 6 existing groundwater well.

The project is largely contiguous to existing linear infrastructure and the pipeline will be installed using a trench method. The project will cross up to 4 temporary graminoid marsh wetlands. There are no known or suspected contaminated sites within the project footprint

No species at risk have been identified, no critical habitat in proximity of the proposed project, and construction activities will take place outside of the migratory bird period of April 15 to August 31. There are no known or suspected contaminated sites within the project footprint.

Indigenous Services Canada is providing funding for the project.

Document.project_name: Aquatic Restoration – Babel Creek, Consolation Lakes, Corral Creek, Fish Creek and Mosquito Creek
location: Detailed Impact Assessment, Banff National Park of Canada
Document.description: Parks Canada proposes to remove non-native fish species from Consolations Lakes and Upper Babel Creek, Corral Creek, Fish Creek and Mosquito Creek in Banff National Park and to reintroduce Westslope cutthroat trout and Bull trout where they were historically present. This proposal considers fish translocation from source populations and long-term monitoring to ensure self-sustaining populations are established in the recipient waterbodies. This aquatics restoration program will occur over a period of ten years (2026 to 2036).

Document.project_name: Mountain Bike Trails Development Project - Valcartier
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) has proposed a project which aims to develop a new mountain bike trail network on Mont Brillant. The project includes a trail network covering between 8 and 15 kilometres. The first stage of the project (2021) is the realization of a master plan through a specialized company. Based on Global Positioning System readings, orthophotos and light detection and ranging readings, the Master plan will include a map of the future-trail network, the necessary drainage network, soil characterization, etc. The Master plan will then allow us to go on a bidding process for the building of the new trails. Depending on the availability of the budgets, the building works will be spread out through 2 or 3 fiscal year.

Document.project_name: Temporary Modular Workplaces (TMW), McNaughton Barracks – CFB Kingston
Wright's Cove East-West Magnetic Range Refurbishment
location: DND East-West Magnetic Signature Range at Wright's Cove, Bedford Basin, Halifax
Document.description: This project will refurbish the existing Wright's Cove East-West magnetic range. 16 sub-sea legacy analog search coils will be replaced by modern digital magnetometers. The magnetometers will be connected via fiber-optic cables (80 metre and 120 metre length cables) to a sub-sea Power Supply and Data Transmitter positioned close to the middle magnetometers (between pedestal 7 & 8). A new fiber optic backbone cable will be laid between the Power Supply and Data Transmitter and the Wright's Cove Range building on shore (approximately 1600 metres of cable that is about 28.6 millimetres in diameter). The legacy copper backbone cable will not be removed from the seabed. It has been there for approximately 20 years. The cables that connected the search coils to this backbone will be removed.

Document.project_name: Medley Extension – 4 Wing Cold Lake
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. The Department of National Defence is expanding a concrete apron and constructing a new asphalt pad at 4 Wing Cold Lake. The proposed estimated 76,000 square meter project will include construction of new aircraft hangars, new administrative building(s), and parking.

Document.project_name: Watershed Sub-System Restoration in Rideemaliyadda DSD, Badulla District, Sri Lanka
Document.description:
The ACCESS – Mihikatha Lanka Project aims to restore 13 priority watershed sub-systems within the Rideemaliyadda Divisional Secretariat Division, Badulla District, Sri Lanka. Physical activities include the rehabilitation and improvement of existing small-scale irrigation infrastructure such as village tanks, bunds, spillways, sluices, irrigation canals, Farm Turn-Outs (FTOs), anicuts (small diversion weirs), and associated access and crossing structures. The works involve desilting, bank and slope stabilization, repair and strengthening of hydraulic structures, and improvements to water flow regulation, without constructing new reservoirs or expanding irrigation networks. The project also includes activities such as watershed restoration, reforestation, soil conservation, invasive species management, strengthening of water governance systems, and climate-resilient livelihood development.

The project area is located in a rural agricultural landscape highly dependent on irrigation systems and characterized by degraded watersheds, significant erosion and sedimentation, aging irrigation infrastructure, increasing climate variability, remnant forest patches, riparian habitats, artificial water reservoirs, and predominantly rice-based agricultural lands.

Document.project_name: Wharf Demolition and Removal at the Lorneville Small Craft Harbour, Saint John County, New Brunswick
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada – Small Craft Harbours

Document.project_name: Rook I Project
Document.description:
NexGen Energy Ltd. (NexGen) is proposing to develop an underground uranium mine on the Patterson Lake peninsula in the southwestern Athabasca Basin in northern Saskatchewan, approximately 155 km north of the town of LaLoche, SK. The proposed Rook l mine would produce up to 14 million kg of U3O8 annually for twenty-four years.

Under the Nuclear Safety and Control Act, NexGen's proposal requires approval and licensing by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC). An environmental assessment (EA) conducted under the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, 2012 is required, and an EA decision affirming that the proposed activities will not cause significant adverse environmental effects, before the CNSC can make a licensing decision on this proposal.

This project is also subject to the environmental assessment requirements of the Government of Saskatchewan.

Document.project_name: Lodge at Bow Lake Contaminated Site Remediation
Document.description: The Lodge at Bow Lake is proposing to remediate contaminated soils from historic fuelling practices at the site between 1970 and 2013. Work will involve the removal of contaminated soils to a licensed landfill, backfilling with clean material and post remediation monitoring.

Document.project_name: New Delivery Centre - Orillia ON
Document.description:
Canada Post Corporation (CPC) is proposing to construct and operate a New Delivery Centre on a 1.31-hectare site at 14-16 Nelle Carter Court in Orillia, Ontario. 

The Project includes a new building of approximately 1,300 square meters.  Pre-construction activities will include exclusion fencing, land clearing, topsoil stripping, sub-excavation, engineered fill, rough grading, and implementation of a soil management plan. The new Delivery Centre is a final sort facility for mail and parcels and will include some office space. The Project site will also include loading and parking spaces for trucks and a trailer, employee parking, landscaping, stormwater management, site lighting, and waste and recycling storage.

Document.project_name: Municipality of Jasper Wastewater Treatment Plant Equalization Pond Reinstatement
Document.description: The Municipality of Jasper Wastewater Treatment Plant has experienced several system failures and service disruptions that resulted in untreated wastewater entering the original lagoon system and subsequently migrating into the underlying rocky substrate. The Municipality of Jasper is proposing to install an appropriate liner system within the existing lagoon cell to provide adequate containment.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff Sulphur Mountain Pipeline and Kootenay Pumphouse Replacement
Document.description: The Town of Banff water services is proposing a new water pipeline to service upper Sulphur Mountain (gondola, hot pools, Rimrock), as well as the replacement of the current pumphouse close to Kootenay Ave. The Town is requesting to install the new watermain adjacent to the existing right of way (ROW) (Fortis Power lines) by widening it permanently by 10 meters (20 m during project, 10 m to be reclaimed afterward). This will allow them to maintain the current water supply to downstream users (PCA, Rimrock, Pursuit), and maintain safe distances from the current ATCO gas line. The pipeline will be installed by open trench for 90% of it's length (the safest method due to other buried utilities), and horizontal directional drilling where open trench is not safe/feasible. The new pipeline will tie into the existing Sulphur Mountain Reservoir located up slope from the PCA Upper Hot Springs. The existing water main will be abandoned in place. The existing Pump Station will be demolished once the new potable main and respective pump station are commissioned. The temporary construction workspace and new pipeline easement will be remediated after completion of pipeline. The Kootenay pump house will be replaced with a new building.

Document.project_name: Wood chip plant remediation - 8501 Ontario Street
location: Wood chip plant remediation - 8501 Ontario Street
Document.description:
Howe Sound Pulp & Paper Corporation (HSPPC) is proposing targeted environmental remediation activities at the former West Coast Chip Plant site located at 8501/8502 Ontario Street, Vancouver. The remediation follows completion of a Detailed Site Investigation (DSI), Detailed Quantitative Human Health and Ecological Risk Assessment (DQHHERA), and Remedial Action Plan (RAP), which identified localized soil and groundwater contamination associated with historical industrial operations. The project is intended to address petroleum hydrocarbons (LEPH/HEPH), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), tetraethyl lead (TEL), localized light non-aqueous phase liquid (LNAPL), and other contaminants through targeted excavation and associated groundwater management.

The proposed works include excavation and off-site disposal of contaminated soils, localized LNAPL recovery, temporary dewatering (if required), confirmatory soil and groundwater sampling, installation of post-remediation monitoring wells, and restoration of excavated areas with clean imported fill. The project also includes decommissioning and removal of the existing stormwater treatment aeration lagoon and associated infrastructure, as well as removal of an associated electrical transformer. Environmental protection measures, including erosion and sediment control, stormwater management, and construction environmental monitoring, will be implemented throughout the remediation program in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

Document.project_name: Maintenance of the dams at Lac à la Pêche and Lac Wapizagonke, La Clairière area
location: La Mauricie National Park of Canada
La Mauricie National Park of Canada
Document.description: The dams at Lac à la Pêche and Lac Wapizagonke (La Clairière sector) require maintenance to ensure their safety and extend their service life. The work includes repairing the caissons and wooden abutments, stabilizing the riprap downstream of the dams and at the shore supports, and controlling vegetation adjacent to and above the abutments and supports.

Document.project_name: Wharf 401 Reconstruction - Millerand Harbour - Magdalen Islands
Document.proponent: Small Craft Harbours  - Fisheries and Oceans Canada
Document.description:
A recent underwater inspection revealed extensive deterioration of exposed wooden com-ponents and bolted assemblies. New cladding or ladders can no longer be safely installed due to the advanced degradation of the existing wood.

Built in 1974, the structure has exceeded its intended lifespan, and partial repairs are no longer viable. A full reconstruction of Wharf 401 is required to ensure the safety of vessels and fishermans.

 
The project includes the following activities:

•    Supply of treated timber, plastic cladding, galvanized hardware, concrete slabs, and ballast stone
•    Partial demolition of the existing creosote treated timber cribwork
•    Proper disposal of demolition materials, including treated and creo-sote contaminated wood
•    Excavation of the seabed to prepare a granular foundation for new cribwork
•    Assembly, launching, placement, and completion of timber cribwork structures
•    Installation of precast concrete slabs, ladders, and fenders
•    Electrical and mechanical upgrades to modernize wharf services

Document.project_name: Fredericton Farm Services Building Replacement Project
Document.description:
Project Description:

Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada intends to build a new 1,326 m2 farm services building and demolish an old 2,060 m2 building at the Fredericton Research and Development Center. The development work will also include: 1. road and parking lot improvements, 2. utility hookups, and 3. building landscaping.

Document.project_name: Shell Beach Erosion Control Project, Portland Island
Document.description: Ongoing monitoring by Parks Canada and First Nations has shown severe erosion at Shell Beach on Portland Island. Parks Canada is proposing a shoreline restoration project to reduce the levels of erosion. The work will involve a soft-armouring approach to dissipate wave action and the revegetation of native plants to further stabilize the shoreline. Parks Canada will complete a basic impact assessment to assess the proposed project's potential impacts to natural and cultural resources. The impact assessment will incorporate standard and site-specific measures to avoid and minimize potential impacts to natural and cultural resources.

Document.project_name: Crown Mountain Coking Coal Project
YYG GSE Area Expansion
Proposed 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet
Document.description:
Construction
The construction of a single storey 477 m2 (5,134 ft2) wood framed commercial building with slab-on-grade foundation. The new commercial building will house two (2) tenants including the Retail Petroleum Outlet with Convenience Store and a quick-service restaurant with drive-thru.

Bio-Physical Environment: A site reconnaissance was conducted on June 10, 2026. The construction and operation are not projected to have any adverse environmental effect.

Human Environment: The proposed 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet is located within the Charlottetown Airport Business Park with a mix of commercial and industrial businesses. The areas immediately adjacent and around the proposed 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet project are vacant commercial business lots at this time.

Operations
The 2026 Retail Petroleum Outlet will include Gas Bar and will include the following petroleum storage and dispensing infrastructure:


	100,000 L petroleum underground storage tank (UST)* with 3 section including:
	
		65,000 L regular gasoline product;
		20,000 L diesel product; and
		15,000 L supreme gasoline product.
	
	
	Four (4) Pump Islands with four (4) Dispensers and ten (10) nozzles.


It should be noted that all petroleum infrastructure (i.e., UST, Pump Island, Dispensers etc.) will be constructed and installed to the latest industry standards to be productive of human health and the environment. The new facility will also have a retail propane exchange outlet associated with the convenience store operation. The new commercial building will use propane heat with the quick service restaurant tenant have separate propane tanks for their operations. Operations at the subject site will be connected to the City of Charlottetown municipal systems to supply potable water and sanitary sewer services. The expected volumes of water to be used by the proposed new facility are expected to be minimal.

Mitigation
During the construction phase, stormwater runoff and sediment control measures will be provided by the site contractor and reviewed by the Construction Project Manager on a regular basis. This will include installing silt fencing, straw bales and other measures as required. All construction debris (including any excess site soils) will be disposed of in a provincially approved manner. Any monitoring wells on the proposed expansion footprint would be decommissioned/relocated as required. During construction and operation (including accidents, potential malfunctions and unplanned events) all municipal, provincial and federal codes, standards and best management practices will be followed.

Document.project_name: Laydown and Logistics areas
Document.description:
The Proposed Project: Laydown and Logistics areas

As part of the Greater Toronto Airports Authority's (GTAA's) Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program, logistics and laydown areas will be constructed on Airport Lands, to facilitate construction needs. The sites will consist of temporary construction trailers, worker parking lot, material laydown, equipment storage, and associated infrastructure to support Airport construction projects.

The sites will undergo a variety of improvements, depending upon the requirements for construction, which are expected to include as required minor excavation, clearing and grubbing, utility removals/relocations including the addition of temporary pole-mounted lighting with overhead power, re-grading, placement of aggregate and compact areas where required, construction trailers, security booths, transportation services for workers, paving and line painting of parking and trailer areas, stormwater management, and other associated infrastructure. No new permanent buildings are proposed. Trailers will be prefabricated units delivered to the site.

Several sustainability best practices will be incorporated into the projects design and implementation for the wider Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program.

Document.project_name: Yellowhead Copper Project
Document.description:
Trekor Metals Limited is proposing the construction, operation, and closure of a new open-pit copper mine located about 150 kilometres northeast of Kamloops, British Columbia. The Yellowhead Copper Project has been designed with a production capacity of 90,000 tonnes of ore per day (up to 32 million tonnes per year) over a 25-year mine life. The project, which would also produce gold and silver, includes a new mill, an approximately 110 kilometre transmission line that would connect to an existing B.C. Hydro substation near 100 Mile House, and a rail load-out facility at an existing site at Vavenby.

British Columbia's Environmental Assessment Office is collaborating with the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada as part of the federal impact assessment of the project. For more information on the EAO's process, please visit EPIC.engage.

 

Please note that the proponent of this project was previously known as Taseko Mines Limited.
